## Goal

The first release carries no known defect a person would meet in its first hour, and its repository passes a security-minded reader's first look: shared state survives sharing, an idle machine doesn't keep its hosted home open, the review layer works inside tabs, every dependency advisory is fixed or explained, releases are signed and carry their provenance, and the runtime's access checks are held by tests that fail if one regresses.

## Owned requirements

None: a maintenance or design unit owns no requirement (D152). Its progress report's evidence table has one row per item of its scope, each closed by a check through the real public interface (README §3), and the checks it adds extend their owners' rows.

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- `share --cloud` carries the artifact's shared state to the hosted copy and hands it back on stop, and never discards it (#232);
- a hosted home whose owner is connected but idle closes after its idle timeout, and `home.activeSeconds` counts work, not connected time (#251);
- the review layer's comments inside tabs and other hidden content: anchors that don't depend on generated ids, the right crop, no marker on unrelated content (#250), and a Comment button that stays readable and still until it's clicked (#257);
- the dependency updates open in Renovate merged, the two `hono` advisories first (#145, #146, #121, #122, #179, #180, #241), every remaining advisory explained in `osv-scanner.toml`, signed release tags, the release's provenance attached to the GitHub release, and the OpenSSF Scorecard re-run;
- two `useField` calls with one field ID share one value without a render loop, and every runtime error about a field names its ID (#233);
- the README's first paragraph and the release notes matched to what the first release ships, for people meeting Mostra for the first time;
- the Skill's guidance that a round of questions on a page is one-off (#254);
- access-control regression tests of the runtime's own checks, from an adversarial review's case list, if confirmed (design detail);
- the runtime-side findings of the adversarial review of a hosted deployment, added to this specification when the review ends.

Design detail for this package:

- A maintenance unit (D152): it owns no requirement. Its scope is the GitHub milestone `MT-08`, each item closed with its check through the real interface (a real `mostra-runtime server` with its fake providers, as WP-30's, MT-05's and MT-06's suites run it) and a test red on the old code; the checks it adds extend their owners' rows. Work the launch blockers first, in the order of the scope list: #232, #251, #250 and #257, the two `hono` advisories, then the rest.
- **#232, shared state across a share.** `share --cloud` sends the artifact's current shared state (every artifact-scope field with its revision) with the share's first push, and the hosted copy starts at that revision, so `mostra state get` and every viewer see the same values before and after. While shared, the hosted copy is the one place state changes; `share stop` brings the hosted fields and revision back into the home before the share ends, and the CLI reads the home again. If the state can't be carried (the server refuses, a field is over a limit), the command refuses with a named diagnostic and changes nothing: it never starts an empty copy and never discards local values. Shares made before this release, whose hosted copy started empty, keep working; their state is whatever the hosted copy holds, and the release notes say so.
- **#251, an idle owner.** The binding touches its home only for messages that carry work (a push, an authoring call, a relayed run, a view, a submission, a state change), not for keep-alive or presence frames; the simplest form is to touch in the protocol's request handlers instead of on every frame. A home with only a connected, idle owner closes after `homes.idleCloseMinutes`, and the owner's next request opens it again as today. `home.activeSeconds` then measures work, which is what an operator that prices or limits by active time needs; MT-05 already makes an open, idle home write nothing, and this is the lifetime and metering side of the same rule. The release notes tell operators that active time drops for idle connected owners.
- **#250, comments inside tabs.** An anchor is stored by what doesn't change between renders and builds: the nearest field ID or `data-mostra-anchor`, else a text quote with its surrounding text, plus a structural path that skips generated ids (`useId`-style ids are never part of it), and the *context* it was made in: the tab panel it sits in (the tab's value and label) or any other hidden container the kit names. A comment whose anchor isn't visible shows no marker; its thread says where it is ("in the tab Round 1"), and opening it brings that place back (the kit's tabs switch to it). The crop is rendered in the same context, with that tab open; if the place can't be reproduced, the crop says so instead of showing another place. Comments made before this release keep their old anchor and resolve it when they can, and never draw a marker on unrelated content.
- **#257, the Comment button.** Readable contrast (WCAG AA) in every state (rest, hover, focus, pressed) in both themes, checked by the shell's contrast test; its position is fixed when the selection ends and doesn't move while the pointer travels to it, so the first click opens the comment box (a Playwright test selects text, moves to the button and clicks once, in each browser).
- **Dependencies and the supply chain.** Merge Renovate's open updates, rebased and tested, `hono` and `@hono/node-server` first because both advisories reach the remote server's request path. Any advisory left (a dev-only path, no fixed version) gets an entry in `osv-scanner.toml` with its reason and a review date, and `osv-scanner` runs in CI against it. **Signed tags:** design it twice and choose (D123): (a) keyless signing in the release workflow (Sigstore's `gitsign`), verified by `git verify-tag` in a later job; (b) an SSH signing key held as a repository secret. Recommended (a): no long-lived key to guard. **Provenance:** the release workflow already makes build attestations; attach each as an `*.intoto.jsonl` asset of the GitHub release, which is what OpenSSF Scorecard's Signed-Releases check reads. Re-run Scorecard and record its score and the checks still below 10 in the progress report, each with a reason or a follow-up issue.
- **#233, one field ID twice.** Two `useField` calls with the same ID, kind, scope and initial type are a deliberate shared value (verify's field lint already says so as a hint): the runtime keeps one value for both and must not loop. A second registration with another kind, scope or initial type is the error verify's lint already names; the runtime's own error for it names the ID and both places instead of a minified React error, so an agent finds it at once.
- **The first reader's view.** The README's first paragraph says what the first release does, without decks, motion or terminal modes, which come after it (D184); the maintainer approves its wording before merge. The release's notes are written for someone meeting Mostra for the first time: what it is, how to try it in one command, what's in this release, and what changed for people who used earlier versions.
- **#254, rounds are one-off.** The Skill's questionnaire guidance teaches it: an answered round is never edited or extended, follow-ups go in a new round that may refer to the earlier one, and news the person should read goes in a status section of the page, not only in chat. Agent-facing prose, drafted with the maintainer (D149, D74).
- **Access-control regression tests, if confirmed.** If the maintainer confirms it (an open question when this was written; otherwise it moves to the next maintenance unit), a suite `tests/security/` holds the runtime's access checks against a real server, each test named for the property it holds: another account's homes, artifacts, routes, files, live channels and MCP handles are refused with the same answer whether or not they exist; a removed artifact's label never serves another account's content; a view-only link can't submit, comment, run actions or read others' answers, a link made for one person can't act as another, and a link reaches only the versions it allows; a short-lived link dies on time on the server; a revoked link ends its shell sessions and open frames within the stated bound, and a rotated secret is dead everywhere; the link secret never appears in a URL or `Referer` after the session exchange; shell tickets are bound to their route and label; an action not opened to anyone with the link refuses anonymous viewers, a run request runs at most once, and a paused artifact refuses runs and submissions with 423; the owner binding refuses revoked, expired and wrong-audience tokens and closes an open connection within a minute of revocation; uploads with a wrong hash, no pending push or over the limit are refused, and file listings with traversal, absolute or look-alike paths are refused; hosted files are served with `nosniff` and never from the API origin; OAuth `state`, PKCE, code reuse and refresh-token reuse behave as INTERFACES §18 says; sign-out refuses other origins; cookies carry their prefixes and flags; malformed requests reveal no stack, path or configuration. Each case that today's code already passes is a guard; any that fails is a finding filed as an issue and fixed in this unit if it blocks the release.
- **Adversarial findings (added Sat Nov 28).** An adversarial review of a hosted deployment, by an outside-view tester and a code-reading tester, ends before this unit starts its last day. Its runtime-side findings are added here, each as an issue in the milestone (label `launch-blocker` where it blocks) with its reproduction, and each closed with a test red on the old code. Until then this section is empty.
- Add MT-08's own decision entry (the share's state hand-over, the anchor's form and context, the signing choice), the dossier text each item changes (INTERFACES §18 for #232 and #251, DATA_MODEL for the anchor), `SECURITY.md` (signed tags and provenance, how to verify them), a changeset whose release notes name each change people see, and the runtime's `AGENTS.md` where the review overlay or the binding changed.

## Out of scope

- New features of any kind: motion, decks and terminal modes come after the first release (D184), homes an organization owns later still.
- An operator's own prices, limits and alerts: MT-08 makes the meter honest; what an operator charges for it is the operator's.
- The flaky-test issues that don't block a release (#39 to #247): they stay with their owners unless one fails the release candidate.
- Comments pinned on several places at once (#256), an idea for later.

## Acceptance evidence

one row per scope item, each closed through the real interface with a test that is red on the old code: #232's reproduction as an integration test through the CLI and a real `mostra-runtime server` (state equal before, during and after a share); an owner connected and idle for twice `homes.idleCloseMinutes` leaves its home closed and its `home.activeSeconds` at most one idle window; a Playwright test per browser that pins a comment inside a non-default tab, checks its crop and that no marker shows on another tab, and selects text and opens the comment box with one click; a page with two `useField` calls on one ID renders and verify passes with its shared-value hint; `osv-scanner` green against `osv-scanner.toml`; a release candidate built from the unit's merge with a verified signed tag and the provenance asset on its GitHub release; Scorecard's report linked from the progress report; each regression test named for the property it holds.

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- #232's hand-over must not lose a write made between the last hosted change and the stop: the stop reads the hosted revision under the same lock that ends the share, and a test races a write against `share stop`.
- #251 changes what active time means for an operator who already reads it: the release notes say so, and the meter's name stays.
- Old comments' anchors (CSS paths through generated ids) can't always be resolved: they degrade to "can't show where", never to a wrong place.
- A dependency update that changes behaviour is found by the full suite, not by its changelog: merge them one at a time on top of the fixes, never as one batch.
- The adversarial findings arrive late in the unit: fix the launch blockers among them first and file the rest for the next unit with a reason.

## Handoff

The first release ships with shared state that survives sharing, an honest meter for idle owners, a review layer that works inside tabs, every advisory fixed or explained, signed tags with provenance, and tests that hold the runtime's access checks. The next maintenance unit takes what the adversarial review filed and this unit didn't block on.
